title: Veins Of Lore
author: Gallamah
description:
“An actual Play Homebrew Dungeons and Dragons Podcast”

“Greetings Everyone and Welcome to Veins of Lore! I’m Brian Judge & I am your Dungeon Master!”

Welcome to our home brew world of Chasmar, 41 years in the making. Full of lore and magic, Gods and Dragons and species familiar and Unique.

I am joined by

My Much more beautiful and better Half Kelsey Middaugh as “Nya Ladyre”  Who is our new blood to D&D

Mike Auriemma as “Ceahcyl Mortesta” in the Main story and "Grhym" for "Rise of the Illgaard" a long-time player of 20+ years

As well as Tim Morgan as “Ulfar the Hexed” in the Main story and "Zaaranth" for "Rise of the Illgaard" another longtime player with 30+ years experience

Joining us for "Rise of The Illgaard" Marc Graff as "Zelus" With 30+  years experience 

 We are a group of lifelong friends that have decided to bring our homebrew world and the experience of every edition of Dungeons & Dragons from Advanced D&D -2014 5e. We are based for the podcast on 2014 5e but we use rulings and calls from every edition we have played through. As well as have many homebrew traditions and rules we bring to the table. There will be times when we make a call based on older rules simply because it may make more sense, while ignoring some mechanics altogether so the story is what tells the tale not the rules.

We are heavy on lore and bring high fantasy to the mic with endearing journeys. Our main focus is the story and where it takes us and you! You will find us heavy on roleplay as well as battle. Some episodes are filled with stories and laughter while others are intense battle and D20 mischief.

We welcome you to join us in the journey of Three Nobles who have been exiled from their home through the deceitful action of a one-time friend who turned into a bitter enemy.

 Join Nya Ladyre the shadow elven barbarian, a divine Zealot favored by the Raven Mother. Her closest childhood friend Ceahcyl Mortesta the Tortle Moon Druid chosen of the mother tree and child of Aurrianna. And their Northman companion Ulfar the Hexed, a Warlock powered by the magic of ancient fey and pact bound to the legendary Sumarbrander.

We take you aboard “The White Ghost’ a great white galleon captained by a High Elven mariner shrouded in intrigue and a mystique all his own. As they race to awaken the powers of an ancient lantern forged in the flames of dragon fire to save the Northern lands of Valkadyr and the Kingdom of Wystere. Tied to the legend of the Hidden Vale and the mysterious druidic stone monoliths that give it its cosmic properties.

All of this and so much more lay in store behind the mic. Laughter and drama are always abroad.

Join us on Podbean, Podchaser, Spotify, Amazon Music, Listen Notes, iheart radio and you tube.

Follow us on Facebook, Tik Tok, and our Sub-reddit. We Are eager to hear from you and interact.

For other unique content you cannot get anywhere else as well as other tidbits and benefits Join our Patreon and subscribe.

Our email is veinsoflore@gmail.com or message us on any of the above media

Thank You and we look forward to sharing our journey with you. SKAL!

If you're a female founder, you might be:

  • Building alone, with no one who sees your vision
  • Feeling unsure of your calling
  • Wondering why progress is taking so long
  • Wondering why it didn't work the first time, and starting again anyway

You'll get business tips to grow your business, encouragement rooted in God's Word, and occasional founder stories with applications you can use right away.

If you're ready to stop trying to figure it out alone, build community with other founders, and trust God on your journey, you're in the right place.

title: Damon Runyon Theater
author: Entertainment Radio
description: Alfred Damon Runyon (October 4, 1880 – December 10, 1946) was an American newspaperman and short story writer. The Damon Runyon Theater radio series dramatized 52 of Runyon's short stories in weekly broadcasts running from October 1948 to September 1949 (with reruns until 1951). The series was produced by Alan Ladd's Mayfair Transcription Company for syndication to local radio stations. John Brown played the character "Broadway", who doubled as host and narrator. The cast also comprised Alan Reed, Luis Van Rooten, Joseph Du Val, Gerald Mohr, Frank Lovejoy, Herb Vigran, Sheldon Leonard, William Conrad, Jeff Chandler, Lionel Stander, Sidney Miller, Olive Deering and Joe De Santis. Pat O'Brien was initially engaged for the role of "Broadway". The original stories were adapted for the radio by Russell Hughes. "Broadway's New York had a crisis each week, though the streets had a rose-tinged aura", wrote radio historian John Dunning. "The sad shows then were all the sadder; plays like For a Pal had a special poignance. The bulk of Runyon's work had been untapped by radio, and the well was deep

McDonald's is one of the most recognizable fast-food brands in the world, serving millions of customers across different countries. But behind its golden arches is a fascinating business story involving ambition, innovation, competition, and an extraordinary vision. This podcast explores how Ray Kroc transformed a small hamburger restaurant into one of the most successful global business empires.

The story begins in 1940, when two brothers, Richard and Maurice McDonald, opened a restaurant in San Bernardino, California. They introduced an innovative system that focused on speed, simplicity, affordability, and consistency. Their approach changed the way people experienced fast food.

Years later, Ray Kroc, a milkshake machine salesman, discovered their restaurant and recognized its enormous business potential. Instead of simply selling equipment, he envisioned something much bigger: a restaurant system that could operate successfully across America and eventually around the world.

Across two episodes, we explore Kroc's entrepreneurial journey, his partnership with the McDonald brothers, the challenges of expansion, the importance of franchising, and the business strategies that made McDonald's a global name.

This is more than a story about hamburgers. It is a lesson in branding, business innovation, leadership, and the power of thinking beyond a single location.

I really want this to be a place where we can all come together. We don’t need to believe the same things, or live the same way, and we don’t have to have everything figured out.

I truly believe that we can love people where they are. I want us to be able to listen to one another without trying to fix each other. We should be able to disagree on things and still care for one another. I really hope we can be honest about our mess and not judge someone else for theirs.

title: Good Life Ahead

description:
Is retirement the end of work, or the start of something new?  After all, curiosity lasts a lifetime, as does the desire for a healthy life, real friendships, and the excitement of the undiscovered.

Good Life Ahead is a weekly show for people entering their next chapter: retirement, fewer responsibilities, children who’ve left the nest; people who want to live fully in this next act.  Host Andrew Motiwalla is that trusted friend who has some tips for what’s around the corner.  He’ll sit down with the experts, authors and tour guides, scientists and researchers, and cultural insiders who can dig in to navigating life’s transitions happily, healthily, and answer the question: what does it really mean to retire?

Woven through Good Life Ahead is Andrew's take on the travel world, the kind of insider intelligence that only comes from being in the industry. This isn't a retirement-planning show, and it isn't a self-help show; it's a weekly sit-down about living well, staying healthy, building community, and learning about the finer things in life.

About the Host, Andrew Motiwalla

Andrew Motiwalla has built an international career around one simple belief: immersive travel and living abroad changes you for the better. It started with a two-year Peace Corps stint in Central America, followed by multiple stretches living abroad. Ever since, he's devoted his career to helping others find that same sense of purpose through meaningful international experiences.
After the Peace Corps, Andrew served as Senior VP at Cross-Cultural Solutions, sending Americans around the world for short-term volunteering. Later, he founded Global Leadership Adventures, a student travel company rooted in global citizenship. When his own children grew older, he wanted to pass those values on directly, so he created Discover Corps, focused on family volunteer travel.
Working with retirees at Discover Corps raised a bigger question for Andrew: what does retirement really mean, and does it have to mean slowing down? He saw that retirement travel and educational travel for seniors weren't just ways to pass time, they were ways to stay curious and build a genuinely active retirement lifestyle. Combined with his own parents' experience thriving in a 55+ community, he fused travel and community to create The Good Life Abroad.

About The Good Life Abroad

The Good Life Abroad is Andrew’s solution to help people realize their dream of living abroad someday - whether for just a month, or longer.  This unique program offers travelers ages 55 and older a combination of vetted apartments, local staff support, and a built-in community of fellow travelers. This allows you to live like a local, but with a safety net, and a network of new friends. 

The Good Life Abroad is Andrew's answer to a simple question: is retirement the end of work, or the start of your best chapter? Through retirement travel ideas, curated destinations, and a community of active adults, he helps people reinvent themselves after retirement, proving it's never too late to start over, and that a purposeful retirement lifestyle abroad is possible at any age.  After working with thousands of travelers at Discover Corps, Andrew realized that many older travelers sought a way to slow down their travel, live like a local, and embrace a different rhythm of life. It was this insight that led to the creation of The Good Life Abroad.  

To learn more about The Good Life Abroad visit our website https://thegoodlifeabroad.com where you can also subscribe to our newsletter. Do you have questions, comments, know the perfect GLA guest or want to be a guest on the show? Reach out to us at podcast@thegoodlifeabroad.com.

title: Mind If I Join You? Special Episode
author: Lundbeck
description:
Mind If I Join You?

This podcast has been organised and funded by Lundbeck and is intended for UK audiences.

Mind If I Join You? is a podcast series for anyone affected by brain health conditions, whether through personal experience, professional life or helping loved ones living with conditions like migraine, anxiety or depression.

In this special episode, NHS paediatric nurse Bridget Coles joins Dr Rebecca Walker, a headache specialist and Senior Clinician at the National Migraine Centre, to explore the realities of living and working with migraine.

Together, they discuss the impact of migraine, from managing symptoms in a demanding healthcare environment to navigating the emotional impact, workplace stigma and challenges of balancing professional and personal life.

Drawing on Bridget’s lived experience and Rebecca’s clinical expertise, they discuss the importance of open conversations, supportive employers, practical workplace adjustments and finding effective ways to manage migraine. Through sharing personal experiences and practical insights, they hope to raise awareness, encourage greater understanding and empower people living with migraine to seek the support they need to live life on their own terms.

You should seek specialist help from a healthcare professional if you are concerned about migraine or your health.

About Bridget Coles

Bridget Coles is an NHS paediatric nurse who began experiencing frequent headaches as a child, which developed into migraines during her teenage years. Four years ago, her migraines became significantly more frequent and debilitating, affecting her career, confidence and everyday life.

In this episode of Mind If I Join You?, Bridget shares the challenges of managing migraine while working in a demanding healthcare environment, the emotional and physical toll of living with an often-invisible condition, and how workplace adjustments, supportive colleagues and learning to advocate for herself have helped her regain a better work-life balance.

About Dr Rebecca Walker

Dr Rebecca Walker is a GP, Associate Specialist in Headache at the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital, and Senior Clinician at the National Migraine Centre. Over her career, Rebecca has developed extensive experience across neuroscience specialities and women's health, giving her a deep understanding of the wide-ranging impact of migraine and a passion for holistic headache care.

Places to look for help

The organisations listed below are not affiliated with the Mind If I Join You? podcast

Migraine Trust – The Migraine Trust is a UK charity that provides information and support for people living with migraine, their friends and families. (www.migrainetrust.org/)

The Brain and Spine Foundation – The Brain & Spine Foundation provides professional information and support for people experiencing neurological conditions living in the UK. (www.brainandspine.org.uk/)

National Migraine Centre – The National Migraine Centre is a charity dedicated to providing diagnosis and treatment for individuals who suffer migraine and other primary headache. (www.nationalmigrainecentre.org.uk/)

title: Spirits from the Top Shelf

description: Every place has a history. Every history leaves its mark. And sometimes, those marks become ghosts. Spirits from the Top Shelf is an immersive journey through the landscapes, history and folklore of some of the world's most intriguing haunted places. Each episode explores the geography and character of a location, meets the people who lived there, and only then encounters the ghost, because behind every haunting lies a story, and often the most compelling mystery is the human events that gave rise to the legend. The series begins in Scotland, inspired by Peter Underwood's A Gazetteer of Scottish Ghosts, found by host Colin on a childhood visit to Edinburgh Castle. Later seasons will travel to Ireland, England, Australia and beyond. Whether you believe in ghosts or simply enjoy a compelling story, pour yourself a wee dram, settle into your favourite chair, and join us.

title: Live from the Living Room

author: Jasper Calcara
description:
Welcome to The Structure of Excellence, a podcast hosted by Jasper Calcara, structural engineer, entrepreneur, and speaker. This is a space for exploring what excellence really looks like and what it takes to build a life that performs at a high level without sacrificing what matters most.
Each episode, Jasper sits down with individuals who have demonstrated excellence in their own unique ways, from entrepreneurs and business leaders to creatives, athletes, and people whose stories challenge traditional ideas of success. Through honest and thoughtful conversations, they explore the experiences, decisions, sacrifices, relationships, setbacks, and defining moments that have shaped them.
Because true excellence isn't just about reaching the top. It's about building a life you actually want to live along the way.
Whether you're building a business, navigating a major life transition, redefining success, or simply looking to live with greater purpose, The Structure of Excellence offers a fresh perspective on what it means to build a life of lasting fulfillment, meaningful contribution, and impact.

From political systems and democracy to social justice, education, human rights, and cultural change, we discuss the important issues influencing everyday life. Discover how governments work, why societies change, and how individuals and communities contribute to building a better future. Through informative discussions, interesting ideas, and real-world perspectives, this podcast makes complex social and political topics easier to understand. Whether you are interested in current affairs, social development, or global challenges, join us to explore the connections between people, politics, and society.

A world that keeps updating. A brain installed in 1981.
Join Irish comedian, dad and former professional wrestler Keego as he questions the news, everyday life and the things we’ve somehow all agreed are normal. Whether you love outdoor adventures, natural wonders, or simply enjoy learning about Earth, this podcast brings you inspiring stories and interesting discoveries from the natural world. author: Joseph Garrette Sr
description: 🎙️ LIGHTEN UP CHURCH PODCASTREAL FAITH. REAL CONVERSATIONS. Our goal isn't to create an echo chamber. It's to encourage meaningful conversations, promote biblical understanding, and remind people that following Christ doesn't mean losing your personality or sense of humor.Whether you're a lifelong believer, questioning religious traditions, recovering from church hurt, or simply looking for authentic conversations about faith and culture, there's a seat at our table for you!🎙️ LIGHTEN UP CHURCH PODCASTSame Truth. Different Conversations.We have fun with our faith while maintaining God's truth!📺 New episodes Sundays at 6 PM Central.📱 Instagram & TikTok: @lightenupchurchpodcast🔔 Follow, subscribe, and join the conversation!

title: THE BLACK LINE
author: GIROLAMO
description: “The Black Line for Life” could be interpreted in various ways, depending on the context. It might symbolize a significant boundary or turning point, akin to a line that separates one phase of life from another. This concept could reflect major life decisions, pivotal moments, or the challenges that shape one's journey. It might also represent the idea of mortality, with the “black line” being a metaphorical marker of life’s finitude. Understanding and respecting this line can inspire individuals to live more purposefully, appreciating each moment and striving to make meaningful contributions. Whether it's a literal or figurative line, it encourages reflection on the paths we choose and the legacy we aim to leave behind.

title: In Practice: Education. Leadership. Impact

From big ideas to real impact. In Practice brings you candid conversations with Harvard alumni, educators, researchers and business leaders about how education shapes the way people think, decide, lead and create impact.

  • Apply their learning in fields such as law, medicine, engineering, policy, entrepreneurship, technology and the arts
  • Credit education as a defining force in their careers

A gathering place for reflective dialogue, meaningful work and the deeper purpose behind leadership.

title: The Practice of Leadership
author: Adam Rampton
description:
Leadership isn’t a title. It’s a practice.
The Practice of Leadership with Adam Rampton explores how executives, founders, and emerging leaders navigate the moments that shape how they lead.

Discover how nature works, why our environment is changing, and how human activities influence the planet. Whether you love science, nature, or environmental discoveries, this podcast makes Earth science interesting, informative, and easy to understand.

title: Tranquility with John Coverstone - for Kids
author: John Coverstone
description: Tranquility now brings you bedtime stories for kids. Let us read your bedtime stories at night and give you a break! We provide gentle stories that are of interest to children, but still lull them into a state of sleep by the soothing voice of veteran podcaster John Coverstone.

title: Conversations with Great Historians
author: The Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History

title: Conversations with Tchiyiwe Chihana

Conversations with Tchiyiwe Chihana explores politics, literature, culture, identity and public life, with particular attention to Africa and its diaspora.
An experienced broadcaster and interviewer, Tchiyiwe speaks with writers, artists, political figures and people whose experiences offer insight into the issues of our time.
The podcast brings together selected interviews from her broadcasting archive and new conversations, with room for curiosity, disagreement, personal reflection and serious discussion.
Follow for new episodes.

title: I'm Glad Someone Said It
author: Sara Wollner
description:
The things we think but don't always say. The feelings we don't know how to explain. The moments you realize, "Wait… it's not just me?"
Hosted by Sara Wollner, wife, mom of two, and someone who's built a community on social media sharing life's honest, messy moments. This podcast is an extension of those conversations — just a little deeper.
From motherhood and grief to relationships and everything in between, expect honest conversations, unexpected laughs, and reminders that you're not alone.
Because sometimes we just need to hear someone else say it. And I'm glad someone said it.

title: Third Place Sessions
author: Carrie Hopperstad and Adam Riehl
description:
Third Place Sessions is a podcast about the places where we gather, connect, and feel like we belong.
Friends and community-builders Carrie Hopperstad and Adam Riehl talk with storytellers, creators, and interesting people about the places that shaped their lives, from yoga studios and neighborhood bars to radio stations, tour buses, online communities, and beyond.
We explore why these places matter and what turns an ordinary space into somewhere you feel known.
Community isn’t just something we find. It’s something we create by showing up, participating, and noticing one another.

title: The Chemistry Lab
author: Sunny
description: The Chemistry Lab explores the fascinating science behind the materials, reactions, and substances that shape our everyday lives. From the elements that build the universe to the chemical processes happening inside our bodies, this podcast makes chemistry interesting, accessible, and easy to understand. Discover scientific discoveries, surprising reactions, and the hidden chemistry behind the world around us.

title: Ageless Performance Podcast
author: Richard W. Hare
description:
Aging is inevitable. Declining performance doesn’t have to be.


Hosted by Richard Hare, the Ageless Performance Podcast explores practical, evidence-informed ways to stay strong, healthy, and capable after 40. We talk about the changes that come with age—and what you can do to support better body composition, strength, energy, and long-term health.


Episodes cover resistance training, nutrition and macros, fat loss while preserving muscle, sleep and recovery, hormones, GLP-1 medications, and strategies for improving healthspan. You’ll hear clear explanations, useful takeaways, and conversations with knowledgeable guests.


The goal isn’t just to live longer. It’s to perform longer. Subscribe and build for the long game.

title: Flowing in God's Purpose by Irwin Brown
author: Momentum Media Advertising
description: Are you tired of paddling hard and still feeling stuck? This eight-episode journey through Irwin Brown's teaching on purpose takes you from striving and spiritual drift to a life carried by God's current. You'll discover what it means to stop forcing your future and start flowing with the One who already knows the way.  By the end of the season, you'll be able to name the hidden blockages that keep you out of the current, including fear, control, comparison, unhealed disappointment, and self-reliance. You'll understand surrender as a doorway to purpose rather than a loss of identity, and you'll learn a practical way to discern God's direction through Scripture, prayer, wise counsel, peace, and circumstances. You'll gain a framework for telling the difference between opposition that confirms you're on course and a warning that you've drifted, along with fresh perspective on waiting seasons as formation rather than wasted time. Finally, you'll leave with a simple daily rhythm of surrender, listening, obedience, patience, and community that you can begin practicing right away.  This season is for the believer who loves God but feels like they're swimming upstream. Maybe you're weary from striving, unsure whether you're hearing God or just your own ambition, or stuck in a long season of silence and delay. Whether you're listening on your commute or reading along, this series was made to help you feel seen, find direction, and move forward with peace.

author: Rufus King
description:
At 8:34 P.M., the lifeless body of Mr. Endicott is discovered, only to face an astonishing twist—by midnight, he's revived with a shot of adrenaline, and by 1 A.M., he’s murdered again. Lieutenant Valcour dives headfirst into a baffling case that challenges the very essence of life and death. "Murder by the Clock" takes you through a gripping timeline filled with unexpected turns, where every suspect holds a secret and every clue leads to more questions.

As Valcour navigates this intricate web of deceit, he relies on his sharp intuition and keen investigative skills to unravel the truth. Is the killer someone from Endicott's past, or does the key lie in the strange circumstances surrounding his revival? With a cast of intriguing characters, each with a motive, Valcour races against time to piece together the mystery before the clock strikes again.

This audiobook offers not just a murder mystery, but a deep dive into human psychology and the lengths people will go to conceal their secrets. With twists that will keep you guessing and a narrative that immerses you in the detective’s journey, "Murder by the Clock" is a must-listen for fans of crime fiction. Join Lt. Valcour as he untangles this chilling enigma, where nothing is as it seems and time is always ticking away.

description:
Are you making an impact, or just surviving the week?

Every teacher starts out wanting to make a difference but somewhere between the endless marking, meetings, and data collection, it's easy to wonder, "Am I really making an impact?"

Welcome to CLASSROOM IMPACT, a podcast for teachers who want to reconnect with why they teach. Hear us explore practical, evidence-informed ways to make every hour in the classroom count.

We're Kylie and Lilia, two Australian primary school teachers (and sisters!) who are passionate about turning research into classroom reality. We know what it's like to feel stretched thin, inspired one day and overwhelmed the next. That's why we created Classroom Impact, to help teachers like us find approaches that work, energise, and sustain us.

Each episode explores:

  • Practical classroom strategies backed by research
  • Ideas that boost student engagement and learning
  • Stories of what's worked (and what hasn't)
  • Real talk about motivation, burnout, and impact
  • Ways to create joy and balance without adding more workload

Watch on YouTube - throw an episode on your classroom smartboard while you prep, mark or pip up artwork.

Listen anywhere - on your commute, while gardening, cleaning or walking (we'll describe any visuals along the way).

Join our growing community of teachers who want to:

  • Reignite purpose and energy in their teaching
  • Make research practical and doable
  • Share honest stories and laughter
  • Create classrooms that truly make an impact

If you're ready to feel inspired, supported, and proud of the difference you make, you're in the right place.

New episodes every month, where we help teachers turn effort into impact that lasts.

From heartbreak and hard living to forgiveness, redemption, and second chances, country music has always had a way of telling the truth about life. And sometimes, those truths point us toward something bigger.


Through laid-back conversations, a little humor, and plenty of good storytelling, Dan and Warren dig beneath the lyrics to discover what these songs can teach us about ourselves, our struggles, and the grace of God.


This isn't a sermon or a traditional Bible study. It's two friends talking about great music, real life, and the places where faith and the human experience intersect.


Because we're all a little bit of a black sheep.

title: The Cardiac Continuum: A Chain Reaction
author: Medscape
description: This six-episode podcast series explores early cardiovascular risk assessment and personalized prevention strategies. Episode 1 frames cardiovascular disease as a cumulative process, emphasizing early intervention and interprofessional care. Episodes 2 and 3 evaluate diagnostic imaging, detailing Coronary Artery Calcium (CAC) scoring and carotid ultrasound to assess vascular age and refine patient risk. Episode 4 covers pharmacological risk management, including lipid-lowering, antihypertensive, and antidiabetic therapies. Episodes 5 and 6 apply these tools to clinical practice through patient case vignettes, comparing imaging modalities to illustrate cost-effective, tailored treatment plans. Throughout the series, interprofessional collaboration drives early, proactive patient care

title: The D.B. Cooper Mystery
author: Shraf
description:
On November 24, 1971, an ordinary-looking man boarded a commercial airplane in Portland, Oregon, using the name Dan Cooper. He appeared calm, dressed in a business suit, and carried a briefcase. Nobody aboard the aircraft could have imagined that this passenger would soon become one of America's most mysterious criminals.

During the flight, the man informed a flight attendant that he had a bomb. He demanded $200,000 in cash and four parachutes. Surprisingly, his demands were met. After releasing the passengers in Seattle, he ordered the aircraft to take off again. Somewhere between Seattle and Reno, he jumped from the rear of the airplane with the ransom money and disappeared into the darkness.

Despite an extensive FBI investigation, hundreds of interviews, and decades of speculation, his real identity and ultimate fate remain unknown.

This two-part true crime series explores the daring hijacking, the mysterious parachute escape, the evidence left behind, and the theories surrounding one of America's most fascinating unsolved criminal cases.

Did D.B. Cooper successfully escape, or did he disappear into the wilderness forever?
